state.question: Why do the four measurement streams show weak or absent cross-correlations and self-correlations, with no clear drift or systematic structure, when properly calibrated instruments in a controlled environment should show either stable agreement or detectable, reproducible divergence?

hypotheses.label: Instrumental independence or environmental decoupling
hypotheses.rationale: The four measurement streams (pendulum_lab, pendulum_obs, resonator_lab, resonator_obs) show negligible cross-correlations even at optimized time lags. All cross-check correlations lie within or near chance level (e.g., pendulum_lab ↔ pendulum_obs: -0.316 vs. ±0.529 chance; resonator_lab ↔ resonator_obs: -0.257 vs. ±0.374 chance). This pattern is consistent with instruments that are genuinely independent—either mechanically decoupled, responding to different environmental variables, or positioned such that they do not share systematic influences. Baseline data show no level shifts (consistent with stable independent operation), and individual means are reproducible within trial. This is not a defect; it is a signature of successful isolation.

hypotheses.label: Measurement resolution or quantization near instrument noise floor
hypotheses.rationale: All four streams show tightly bunched distinct values (pendulum_lab: 144 distinct in 166 trials; others: 57–58 distinct in 60 trials) with smallest spacings of 0.0001. This suggests instruments are resolving signals at or near their thermal/mechanical noise limit. At such resolution, correlations between independent noise sources would be weak or absent by definition.
